record.original_question: Does there exist an infinite family of semigroup conjugacy relations that are first-order definable, that agree with ordinary group conjugacy on every group, and that form an antichain under inclusion, so that no one of the relations contains another?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.21 from [3] asks whether there exists an infinite set of first-order definable conjugacies that forms: (1) a chain ordered by inclusion or (2) an anti-chain ordered by inclusion.
We give a partial answer by constructing an infinite chain of first-order definable conjugacies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A semigroup conjugacy is a binary relation $\sim$ on semigroups, defined uniformly across the class of all semigroups, such that:
(i) for every semigroup $S$, the relation $\sim_S$ on $S$ is an equivalence relation;
(ii) whenever $S$ is a group, $\sim_S$ coincides with the usual group-theoretic conjugacy relation $\{(a,b) : \exists g\in S,\ b = g^{-1}ag\}$.
Such a conjugacy is called first-order definable if there is a first-order formula $\varphi(x,y)$ in the language of semigroups (a single binary operation symbol) such that for every semigroup $S$ and all $a,b\in S$,
$$ a \sim_S b \iff S \models \varphi(a,b). $$
The collection of all first-order definable semigroup conjugacies is partially ordered by inclusion: $\sim \,\le\, \approx$ means that $a\sim_S b$ implies $a\approx_S b$ for every semigroup $S$ and all $a,b\in S$.

Question. Does there exist an infinite antichain in this partial order? That is, does there exist an infinite family $\{\sim^{(i)} : i\in I\}$ of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies such that for all distinct $i,j\in I$ neither $\sim^{(i)} \,\le\, \sim^{(j)}$ nor $\sim^{(j)} \,\le\, \sim^{(i)}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work constructs an infinite chain of first-order definable semigroup conjugacies, giving a partial answer to the original two-part problem (chain or antichain). The antichain part of the question does not appear to have been resolved in the located sources, so it remains open.
